brief: This is a procedural item: reports from the standing committees and boards, and new business from city officials, are introduced to City Council. No decisions are taken.

title: Confirmation of Minutes

title: Tenant Support Grant Program Updates
brief: At its meeting on November 23, 2020, the Subcommittee on the Protection of Affordable Rental Housing considered Item RH4.1, a report (November 4, 2020) from the General Manager, Shelter, Support and Housing Administration on Tenant Support Grant Program Updates. The Tenant Defence Fund (TDF) was created in late 1999 in response to the creation of the Provincial Tenant Protection Act, 1997. City Council is asked to repeal City of Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 797, Tenant Support Grant Program.

title: Creating Affordable Rental Homes at the West Don Lands - Update
brief: In October 2017, City Council approved Open Door Program incentives for up to 390 affordable rental housing units to be constructed on the eight-acre site known as Blocks 8/20 and Blocks 3W, 4W and 7W in the West Don Lands under the Provincial Affordable Housing Lands Program. In May 2019, City Council approved Open Door Program incentives for an additional 33 affordable rental units, plus an extension of the affordability period from 49 to 99 years. City Council is asked to authorize that up to 275 additional affordable rental units to be constructed on the lands known as Blocks 8/20 and Blocks 3W, 4W and 7W in the West Don Lands be exempt from the payment of development charges, building permit, planning application and parkland dedication.

title: RentSafeTO (Apartment Building Standards): Colour-coded Rating System, By-law Amendments, and Program Updates
brief: As directed by City Council in November 2019, this report proposes the creation of a colour-coded rating system for apartment buildings in Toronto and responds to outstanding directives related to the RentSafeTO program. This report was initially expected at the Planning and Housing Committee in April 2020, but was delayed as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic. City Council is asked to amend Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 354, Apartment Buildings, as follows.

title: New User Fee for Employment Areas Conversion Requests
brief: The City's Official Plan Growth Plan Conformity and Municipal Comprehensive Review (MCR) commenced on August 4, 2020. The Work Plan adopted by City Council defines a year-long window between which City staff will receive formal written requests to convert lands designated as Core Employment Areas and General Employment Areas. City Council is asked to amend City of Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 441, Fees and Charges and Chapter 442, Fees and Charges, Administration of, to establish a new Employment Areas Conversion Request User Fee of $20,000 per conversion request received from December 18, 2020.

topics: emergency housing; emergency shelters; homeless shelters; hostels (homeless)

brief: In July 2019, the applicant proposed a 44-storey, 131.9-metre residential building at 40 and 44 Broadway Avenue, with a 4-storey base including a place of worship. Staff recommend that City Council direct the City Solicitor and planning staff to attend the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal and oppose the application in its current form.
address: 40 Broadway Toronto Ontario; 44 Broadway Toronto Ontario

title: Refusal Report - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - 36-44 Eglinton Avenue West
topics: redevelopment, rezoning, zoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: Staff recommend that City Council refuse the zoning amendment application for a 65-storey, 220-metre mixed-use building at 36–44 Eglinton Avenue West, with 663 homes and 550 square metres of retail and office space. The refusal report sets out the planning reasons. Council is also asked to authorize the City Solicitor to defend the refusal at the planning tribunal.

title: Final Report - Application to Lift Holding Provision (H) - 57, 59 and 60 Mobile Drive and 30 Old Eglinton Avenue
topics: redevelopment, zoning; rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: Staff recommend lifting the Holding symbol on the zoning for 57, 59 and 60 Mobile Drive and 30 Old Eglinton Avenue, which currently limits office uses on the lands. Removing it would allow a 3-storey office building to be developed. City Council is asked to amend the former North York zoning by-law.
address: 57-60 Mobile Toronto Ontario; 30 Old Eglinton Toronto Ontario

title: Representation at the Toronto Local Appeal Body for 160 Ellerslie Avenue
topics: appeals, legal matters; legal issues
brief: The Committee of Adjustment approved minor variances for 160 Ellerslie Avenue to build a rear one-storey addition, a deck and a west-side two-storey addition. Councillor John Filion recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body and oppose the approval, including any further variances requested.

title: Don Mills Centre - Extension of Section 37 Terms
topics: community benefits;
brief: Deputy Mayor Denzil Minnan-Wong recommends that North York Community Council instruct the City Solicitor and planning staff to report jointly to the October 27, 2020 Council meeting on the Section 37 agreement for the Don Mills Centre. The 2011 Ontario Municipal Board approval implemented Council's settlement for redeveloping the southern Don Mills Centre lands with a local park and public benefits.
address: 49 The Donway Toronto Ontario; 75 The Donway Toronto Ontario

title: Application to Remove a Private Tree - 214 Snowdon Avenue
topics: privately-owned trees, tree removal; private owned trees; private trees; privately owned trees; trees on private property
brief: Staff ask City Council to deny a permit to remove a privately owned tree on the boundary between 214 and 216 Snowdon Avenue. The owner of 214 Snowdon Avenue cites concerns about damage to a deck, the tree's closeness to the house, and potential root damage. The General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation recommends denial.

title: Assumption of Services, Orchard Ridge (Heathview) G.P. Inc., Plan 66M-2501, Subdivision File: 10 264766 NNY 24 SB, 50 Page Avenue
topics: assumption of services, subdivision (land); subdivision of land
brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend that City Council formally assume the municipal services installed under the 2012 subdivision agreement with Orchard Ridge (Heathview) G.P. Inc. for Plan 66M-2501 at 50 Page Avenue — including the services in Valliere Place and the road itself — and release the related securities.

title: Final Report - Zoning Amendment Application - 755 Steeles Avenue West
topics: redevelopment, rezoning, zoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: Staff recommend approving a development at 755 Steeles Avenue West: a 10-storey, 124-unit residential building, twenty-eight 4-storey stacked back-to-back townhouses, and a 1-storey retail building, on the site of an existing 15-storey apartment. The proposal includes 606 square metres of new City parkland, 1,100 square metres of public open space, and improvements to the existing rental building. City Council is asked to approve the zoning amendments.

title: Fulfilling a 'Half-Pipe' Dream: Request to Install a Skateboarding Pad in Christie Pits - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: parks, skateboarding; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, skate boards; skateboards
brief: Councillors Mike Layton and Joe Cressy move that City Council ask the Parks General Manager to work toward installing a skate spot in Christie Pits, in line with the City's Skateboard Strategy. Since summer 2018, residents have run a popular do-it-yourself skate park inside the Sid Smith Rink, which has become a valued space especially for women and youth.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from a Development at 1 and 3 Sultan Street to Fund the Creation and Installation of a Heritage Plaque at 406 Bloor Street East, Commemorating the Underground Railroad Soul Food Restaurant - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam
topics: councillors, food, funding, heritage designation, operating budgets, plaques, railways, restaurants; aldermen; alderwomen; city councellors; city councillors; council members; councilors; members of council, cafeterias; dining; eating places; food premises, financing, heritage plaques; heritage toronto plaques; historic markers; historic plaques; historical markers; local markers; provincial plaques, menus, rail fares; railroads
brief: Councillors Mike Layton and Kristyn Wong-Tam move to release $7,500 in Section 37 development funds to Heritage Toronto for a plaque at 406 Bloor Street East commemorating the Underground Railroad soul food restaurant, which opened there in 1969. It was one of the city's first major southern comfort food restaurants and a hot spot for Toronto's Black culture. The budget increase is fully funded by the Section 37 funds, with no net cost to the City.
address: 406 Bloor Toronto Ontario; 1 Sultan Toronto Ontario; 3 Sultan Toronto Ontario

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 funds to fund the Production and Installation of a Heritage Plaque to Commemorate the History of Toronto’s First Organized Ambulance Service - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Councillors Kristyn Wong-Tam and Shelley Carroll move to release $7,500 in Section 37 development funds to Heritage Toronto for a plaque at 10 Court Street commemorating Toronto's first organized ambulance service, established in 1832 during the city's first cholera epidemic. The budget increase is fully funded by the Section 37 funds, with no net cost to the City.

title: Keeping Sailors Afloat - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: boat facilities, councillors, leasing, local government structure, parks, property taxes, sailing, urban forestry, waterfronts; aldermen; alderwomen; city councellors; city councillors; council members; councilors; members of council, boat slips; facilities for boaters; boat moorings; facilities for boats; anchoring; boating facilities; boat docks; moorin, city council structure; committee structure; council committee structure; council structure; council-committee structure; governance structure, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, forestry; tree health, lakefronts; waterfront trail, leases, municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts
brief: Councillors Paula Fletcher and Brad Bradford move that City Council direct real estate staff to engage community sailing clubs and explore changing waterfront boating facility leases from fully net to semi-gross leases, and report back to the licensing committee. The not-for-profit clubs provide affordable on-water recreation at no cost to the City.

title: Creating a Chain Store Retail Strategy for Toronto - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: businesses, economic development; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing, commercial waste collection customers
brief: Councillors Kristyn Wong-Tam and Mike Layton move a follow-up to Council's 2017 request for a chain store retail strategy, which staff have not yet reported back on. Council is asked to have the Chief Planner, with Economic Development and the recovery office, report to the Planning and Housing Committee in the second quarter of 2021 on a retail strategy protecting neighbourhood character and small businesses.

title: 3655 Kingston Road - Request for Representation at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford
topics: appeals, zoning;
brief: The Committee of Adjustment refused minor variances for a 9-storey apartment building at 3655 Kingston Road in September 2020, and the applicant has appealed to the Toronto Local Appeal Body. Councillors Paul Ainslie and Gary Crawford move that City Council direct the City Solicitor and planning staff to attend the hearing and support the refusal.

title: Implementation of the Federal Rapid Housing Initiative - by Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão
topics: federal governments, housing; homes; residences
brief: Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão, moves that City Council adopt the Housing Secretariat and real estate recommendations to implement the federal Rapid Housing Initiative in Toronto. The initiative, announced September 21, 2020, provides $1 billion nationally through CMHC to rapidly build affordable rental housing for vulnerable and marginalized people.

title: Urging Continued Federal Government Action on Gun Violence - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Mayor John Tory
topics: abuse, crime, firearms; assault; domestic violence; violence, gun licences; gun registration; guns, illegal activity
brief: Councillors Brad Bradford and Mayor John Tory move that City Council thank the federal government for May 2020 orders banning some 1,500 assault weapon models, and express support for making the ban permanent. The motion cites 195 shooting-related deaths in Toronto so far in 2020, including a 21-year-old killed in an LCBO parking lot.

title: Protecting Public Interest and Requesting Accountability from Minister's Zoning Orders - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
brief: Councillors Kristyn Wong-Tam and Joe Cressy move that City Council express its displeasure with the province for issuing three Minister's Zoning Orders for West Don Lands sites — O. Reg. 594/20, 595/20 and 596/20 — on October 23, 2020 without notifying councillors or City Planning staff, who discovered them by chance. The motion also seeks accountability on how the orders will be implemented.

title: Agreement for St. Lawrence Market Grocery Delivery Service - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson
topics: service delivery;
brief: Councillors Kristyn Wong-Tam and Michael Thompson move that City Council authorize the real estate executive to negotiate an agreement with Inabuggy Incorporated for online ordering and grocery delivery service at St. Lawrence Market. The agreement would let Inabuggy use the City's St. Lawrence Market marks in an online store, better serving market tenants and residents.

title: Process to Select and Open Temporary Sites for Physical Distancing in Shelters - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: emergency housing; emergency shelters; homeless shelters; hostels (homeless)
brief: Councillors Anthony Perruzza and Frances Nunziata move that City Council direct the City Manager to report to the November 25, 2020 Council meeting on the process used to open a shelter at the Holiday Inn at 30 Norfinch Drive on May 17, 2020. The motion asks for clarity on how temporary physical-distancing shelter sites are selected and opened.

title: 625 Runnymede Road, 274 St. John's Road, and 40 Fisken Avenue - Zoning Amendment - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: zoning;
brief: Councillors Gord Perks and Joe Cressy move that City Council adopt the Chief Planner's recommendations to fix a minor error in zoning by-laws 642-2020 and 643-2020 for 625 Runnymede Road, 274 St. John's Road and 40 Fisken Avenue. Council approved the by-laws in July 2020 to permit a five-storey long-term care addition to the Runnymede Health Care Centre.
address: 625 Runnymede Toronto Ontario; 274 St Johns Toronto Ontario

title: 57 Florence Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor John Filion, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: appeals, planning;
brief: The Committee of Adjustment approved and modified a minor variance for 57 Florence Avenue, for maximum building height for a proposed new dwelling. The owner has appealed the decision to the Toronto Local Appeal Body. Councillors John Filion and Shelley Carroll move that City Council authorize the City Solicitor to attend the hearing, support the committee's decision and oppose the owner's appeal.

title: Restaurants and Insurance - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: food and beverage industry, insurance; bonding; health coverage, food and beverage cluster; food and beverage sector; food business; food industry
brief: Councillors Paula Fletcher and Joe Cressy move that City Council ask the Ontario government to immediately legislate against insurance companies terminating existing policies for restaurant owners and the hospitality sector. Longstanding restaurants with no claims history face hiked premiums and cancelled policies during the pandemic over COVID-19 liability fears.

title: 103 Overbrook Place - Development Charges Pre-Payment Agreement - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: development; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Councillors James Pasternak and Mike Colle move that City Council allow an amending development charge agreement between the City and Sage 147 Elder Realco, owner of 103 Overbrook Place, so all development charges for the site can be pre-paid. The lands are being developed as a 20-suite addition to the existing 50-suite retirement home at 147 Elder Street, which serves seniors with dementia and cognitive impairments.

title: Too Fast, Too Furious: Addressing Street Racing - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Deputy Mayor Denzil Minnan-Wong
topics: speed limits, traffic violations; demerit points; speeding tickets
brief: Councillors Shelley Carroll and Deputy Mayor Denzil Minnan-Wong move that City Council direct the City Manager to convene an action table with stakeholders to address the sharp rise in street racing on local streets and highways during the pandemic. The motion cites significant traffic safety risks and excessive nighttime noise across the Greater Toronto and Hamilton Area.

title: Lawrence Heights Safety and Security Task Force - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Mark Grimes
topics: safety, security; public safety
brief: Councillors Mike Colle and Mark Grimes move that City Council support creating a Lawrence Heights Community Safety and Security Task Force, after more than 40 reported shootings in the community in the past year — including the October 7, 2020 drive-by murder of Shane Shannon Stanford. The task force would bring together the City, police, Toronto Community Housing and community agencies to address the escalation of violence.

title: Request to Extend the Construction Funding Agreement for Improvements to James Canning Gardens - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: community gardens, funding; financing
brief: Councillors Kristyn Wong-Tam and Mike Layton move that City Council authorize the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to extend the construction funding agreement with The Clover on Yonge Inc. for the James Canning Gardens park improvements to August 31, 2021. The developer's Section 37 agreement required it to design and build the park upgrades.

title: Expanded Free Green P Parking Support on Eglinton Avenue West - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão
topics: parking;
brief: Councillors Mike Colle and Ana Bailão move that City Council ask the Toronto Parking Authority to study expanding the Green P app program to include a free parking voucher for shoppers and residents who cannot use the app. About 140 stores on Eglinton Avenue West have closed as eight years of Crosstown construction blocks access and removes on-street parking.

title: 2228 Bloor Street West - Liquor Licence Application -  Village Juicery Licence 1002918 - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: This is a procedural item: an application has been made to Ontario's alcohol regulator for a liquor licence for Village Juicery at 2228 Bloor Street West, for an indoor area only. Councillors Gord Perks and Mike Layton move that Council tell the regulator the licence is not in the public interest unless conditions addressing residents' concerns are imposed.

title: Reopening Council Decision on Item 2020.EY16.12 in order to permit a further time-extension of Temporary Traffic Regulation, Finch Avenue West at Elana Drive - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: light rail transit, public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation, lrt
brief: Councillors Anthony Perruzza and James Pasternak move to re-open Council's July 2020 decision on temporary traffic regulations at Finch Avenue West and York Gate Boulevard / Elana Drive, and extend them from November 1, 2020 to May 31, 2021. The regulations include restricting the westbound left turn and keeping the southbound through movement.

title: 1906 - 1930 Weston Road - Development Charge Early Payment Agreement - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão
topics: charges, development, development charges; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Councillors Frances Nunziata and Ana Bailão move that City Council authorize a development charges early payment agreement for the rental housing proposal at 1906–1930 Weston Road. Provincial changes effective January 1, 2020 require rental housing development charges to be paid in six equal annual installments over five years from occupancy, and the agreement would set the payment terms.

title: Delivering for Toronto Restaurants: Requesting a Cap on Food Delivery Service Fees - by Councillor Michael Ford, seconded by Mayor John Tory
topics: food, service delivery; menus
brief: Councillor Michael Ford, seconded by Mayor John Tory, moves that City Council ask the Ontario government to put a temporary cap on the commissions food delivery companies charge restaurants. The motion notes restaurants are among the hardest-hit businesses in the pandemic and delivery fees cut deeply into their margins.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 funds to fund the Production and Installation of a Heritage Plaque to Commemorate the History of the Underground Railroad Restaurant on King Street East - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: plaques; heritage plaques; heritage toronto plaques; historic markers; historic plaques; historical markers; local markers; provincial plaques
brief: Councillors Kristyn Wong-Tam and Mike Layton move to release $7,500 in Section 37 development funds to Heritage Toronto for a plaque commemorating the Underground Railroad soul food restaurant, which opened at 406 Bloor Street East in 1969 and moved to 225 King Street East in 1973. The restaurant was one of the city's first major southern comfort food spots and a hub of Black culture. The budget increase is fully funded by the Section 37 funds, with no net cost to the City.

title: Maximizing Municipal Uses to Include Affordable Housing on Existing Community Centre Sites  - by Councillor Cynthia Lai, seconded by Mayor John Tory
topics: affordable housing, cultural facilities, urbanization; affordable homes; housing projects, art centres; arts centres; cultural attractions; cultural centres, intensification; reurbanization
brief: Councillor Cynthia Lai, seconded by Mayor John Tory, moves that City Council direct the Chief Planner, with CreateTO, real estate, housing and parks staff, to explore intensifying existing City-owned lands — including community centre sites — for affordable housing and cultural uses. The motion picks up the recovery report's recommendations on City-owned land.

title: Empowering Toronto with a City Charter - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor John Filion
topics: legislation, municipal councils; acts, city councils
brief: Councillors Josh Matlow and John Filion move that City Council ask the federal government for a mechanism letting Toronto and other municipalities establish a city charter with authority over local matters such as public health. The motion argues the 19th-century constitutional framework constrains cities, and cites the province's recent meddling in municipal elections, including banning ranked ballots.

title: Requesting a Review of Chapter 466, Fireworks - by Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford
topics: fireworks; firecrackers
brief: Councillors Mark Grimes and Gary Crawford move that City Council direct Municipal Licensing and Standards and Toronto Fire Services, with relevant divisions, to review Chapter 466 on fireworks and report the outcome to the General Government and Licensing Committee. The review covers fireworks sales and discharge rules, vendor permits, and enforcement.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 funds to fund the Revitalization of Wellington Street East - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: business improvement areas; business improvement associations; BIA
brief: Councillors Kristyn Wong-Tam and Joe Cressy move that City Council add $343,633.72 in Section 37 development funds to the Wellington Street East streetscape revitalization, raising the project budget from $1,100,000 to $1,443,633.72. Work on the Yonge-to-Church streetscape, underway for about a decade, is tendered to begin in spring 2021 but came in over budget. The increase is fully funded by the Section 37 funds, with no net cost to the City.

title: Council Member Appointment to the Toronto Transit Commission Board - by Deputy Mayor Denzil Minnan-Wong, seconded by Mayor John Tory
topics: board members, councillors; aldermen; alderwomen; city councellors; city councillors; council members; councilors; members of council
brief: Deputy Mayor Denzil Minnan-Wong, seconded by Mayor John Tory, moves that City Council appoint a member of Council to fill the current council-member vacancy on the TTC board, to keep the board governing effectively and avoid quorum issues. The term would end November 14, 2022. The City Clerk has canvassed interested members, including Councillor Paul Ainslie.

title: Representation on the Toronto Transit Commission Board - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson
topics: Toronto Transit Commission; ttc
brief: Councillors Shelley Carroll and Michael Thompson move that City Council ask the Civic Appointments Committee to make every effort to fill the TTC board's public member vacancy with a member of the Black, Indigenous and People of Colour community, giving preference to transit riders. The motion follows the recovery office's recommendation on Black and Indigenous representation in City decision-making.

title: Preserving Ranked Ballot Elections - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: elections, provincial governments; polls (elections); voting
brief: Councillors Shelley Carroll and Joe Cressy move that City Council ask the Ontario government to withdraw its ranked-ballot amendment to the Municipal Elections Act. On October 20, 2020, the province tabled Bill 218, which revokes the framework letting municipalities use ranked ballots. The motion argues municipalities should decide for themselves.

title: Supporting Taxi Operators from COVID-related Financial Hardship - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: communicable diseases, taxicab drivers; infectious diseases, taxi drivers; cabbies; cab drivers
brief: Councillors Kristyn Wong-Tam and Paul Ainslie move to support Toronto's taxicab industry, which has lost over 90 percent of its business to COVID-19 with about 95 percent of the fleet parked. Council is asked to have the City Manager consider reducing 2020 taxicab licensing renewal fees as part of the October 2020 COVID-19 financial report, and to have the licensing committee review further supports.

title: Emergency Road Repair on York Downs Drive, East of Bathurst Street
brief: Councillor James Pasternak recommends that the Infrastructure and Environment Committee ask City Council to direct the General Manager of Transportation Services to assess and carry out emergency road repairs and pothole patching on York Downs Drive, east of Bathurst Street, and meet with the local councillor. The street's resurfacing is bundled with a Toronto Water watermain project scheduled for 2023.

title: Non-Competitive Contract for a New Weigh Scale Solution with Paradigm Software, LLC
topics: committee meetings, contracts, environmental plans, infrastructure, software, solid waste management, system software; computer programs, environment plans, solid waste management planning; swm; waste management
brief: Staff seek City Council authority for the General Manager of Solid Waste Management Services to negotiate a non-competitive contract with Paradigm Software, LLC to implement and support a modernized weigh scale solution for the City. The contract is worth up to $3,523,040 net of HST ($3,585,046 net of HST recoveries), including initial capital costs. No competitive bidding is proposed.

title: Front Yard Parking Regulations and Electric Vehicle Charging on Residential Streets
topics: committee meetings, electric scooters, environmental plans, infrastructure, motor vehicles, parking pads, regulations; boulevard parking; front yard parking; off street parking; off street permit parking, environment plans, go peds; go-peds; motorized scooters; scooters, vehicles
brief: Front-yard parking pads on City boulevards were originally meant for residents with no on-site parking, but rules have been adjusted over time for area characteristics. Staff recommend that City Council ask the General Manager of Transportation Services, as part of the Parking Strategy, to review residential front-yard and commercial boulevard parking — considering electric vehicle charging, tree canopy, stormwater, urban design and safety impacts.

title: Freight and Goods Movement Strategy
topics: carriers (transportation);
brief: Staff ask City Council to approve the Freight and Goods Movement Strategy, which builds on the 2017 framework to support goods movement industries with a Complete Streets approach — strengthening Toronto's economic competitiveness while supporting neighbourhoods. Council is also asked to forward the report to the Toronto Police Services Board to explore better commercial vehicle enforcement with Transportation Services.

title: Request to get Bike Lanes in Midtown along Yonge Street
topics: bike lanes; bicycle lanes; on street bike lanes
brief: Councillor Mike Colle recommends that the Infrastructure and Environment Committee ask Transportation Services to include a temporary protected bikeway on Yonge Street, from south of St. Clair Avenue, in either the 2021 cycling network plan update or the pandemic cycling expansion plan. The motion argues ActiveTO's bikeways must now reach Midtown.

title: Response to COVID-19: Update on Resurgence
topics: disease outbreaks, public health; epidemics; pandemics
brief: Toronto Public Health reports a significant surge in COVID-19 cases, concentrated among younger people living or socializing in downtown neighbourhoods — a shift from the first wave. The Medical Officer of Health recommends that Council and the Board of Health urge Ontario's health ministry to ensure the new provincial Case and Contact Management software meets Toronto Public Health's needs, including identifying clusters for targeted action.

title: Lease Amendments - 419-425 Coxwell Avenue
topics: aboriginal services, affordable housing, leasing, rental housing; affordable homes; housing projects, leases, rental properties; rental units
brief: Staff seek authority to amend the 2002 ground lease with New Frontiers Aboriginal Residential Corporation at 419–425 Coxwell Avenue so the tenant can refinance and redevelop the property. The building currently provides 74 affordable rental units, and the restructuring would let the tenant add 12 more affordable units. City Council is asked to authorize the lease amending agreement.

title: Proposed Land Lease for Part of the City-owned Property at 311 Staines Road to the Tamil Community Centre
topics: community centres, leasing, real estate transactions; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, leases
brief: The City bought 311 Staines Road in 2007 on condition the lands stay naturalized. Staff update Council on non-binding discussions with the Tamil Community Centre about a land lease for the south parcel, separated from the north parcel by a hydro corridor. City Council is asked to authorize the real estate executive to advance the lease discussions with CreateTO, Economic Development, Planning and Parks staff.

title: Community Space Tenancy Lease Agreement and Municipal Capital Facility Designation for Midaynta Community Services at 1652 Keele Street
topics: agreements, commercial tenants, committee meetings, immigrants, leasing, licences, local government structure, non-profit organizations, programs, youth; adolescents, city council structure; committee structure; council committee structure; council structure; council-committee structure; governance structure, immigration status; newcomers, leases, licenses; licensing, non profit; nonprofit; not-for-profit organizations, tenancy agreements
brief: Midaynta Community Services is a non-profit providing settlement services and social and cultural programs for newcomers, immigrants and youth, with over 25 years of work in the Somali Canadian community. Staff recommend that City Council authorize a five-year community space tenancy lease for Midaynta at 1652 Keele Street under the Community Space Tenancy Policy.

title: Co-location of Housing and Service Integration at 2950 and 2970 Lake Shore Boulevard West
topics: administration, capital budgets, committee meetings, housing, land acquisition, licences, local government structure, social assistance; city council structure; committee structure; council committee structure; council structure; council-committee structure; governance structure, financial assistance; income assistance; ontario works; ow; welfare, homes; residences, land acquisitions; park acquisition; parkland acquisition; parks acquisitions; property acquisition; property acquisitions, licenses; licensing
brief: This is an information item: in July 2020, Council approved buying 2950 and 2970 Lake Shore Boulevard West for a municipal shelter and asked staff to consider co-locating permanent housing on the site. The General Manager reports back on the co-location of housing and service integration. City Council is asked to receive the report for information.
address: 2950 Lake Shore Toronto Ontario; 2970 Lake Shore Toronto Ontario

title: Renewal of Proprietary Technology Maintenance Contracts Supporting the City Services from 2021-2025
topics: by-laws, contracts, information and communication technology, municipal services; bylaws, city services, ict; information and communication systems; information and technology; information technology; it
brief: Staff seek authority to renegotiate and renew 186 non-competitive contracts for maintenance of proprietary technology — software, hardware and subscriptions that support City services — for five years from January 1, 2021 to December 31, 2025. The maintenance keeps the City's systems running under its strategic plan. City Council is asked to grant the renewal authority, subject to budget approval.

title: Bridletowne Community Hub - Update
topics: agreements, funding, hospitals, leasing, special purpose bodies; abccs; abcds; agencies; boards; commissions; committees of management; local boards, financing, leases, tenancy agreements
brief: In 2017, Council authorized ground leases with Scarborough Rouge Hospital and the YMCA of Greater Toronto to develop the Bridletowne Community Hub. Staff now ask Council to authorize amended terms and to let the Deputy City Manager and real estate staff execute the ground lease with the Scarborough Health Network on the City's behalf.

title: City Hall Leases for Media Offices
topics: city halls, committee meetings, government services, leasing, licences, media relations, offices, press gallery, tenants; leases, licenses; licensing, media contacts; media kits, renters; tenancy agreements
brief: Staff seek authority to enter into leases with the ten media tenants of the City Hall Press Gallery for five years, from January 1, 2019 to December 31, 2023, with an option to extend five more years. In 2009, Council authorized below-market rents for the press gallery tenants. City Council is asked to authorize the leases, including with future tenants if vacancies occur.

title: Toronto Island Marina - Lease Extension
topics: agreements, attractions, committee meetings, funding, leasing, licences, municipal councils, rent; city councils, cultural attractions; places of interest; tourist attractions; tourist sites, financing, leases, licenses; licensing, rents, tenancy agreements
brief: The Toronto Island Marina leases about 27.58 acres in Toronto Island Park under a lease expiring October 14, 2025, and operates under a management agreement with the Island Yacht Club. Staff recommend that City Council authorize extending the marina's lease by about five years, to July 31, 2030.

title: Community Safety Zone - Mount Olive Drive - Housekeeping Amendment
topics: community safety;
brief: This is a housekeeping item: Mount Olive Drive, between Kipling Avenue and Gihon Spring Drive, is a 40 km/h collector road fronting homes and several schools, designated as a community safety zone. Etobicoke York Community Council is asked to rescind the existing zone between Canve Crescent and Kipling Avenue and designate a corrected zone between Vange Crescent and Kipling Avenue. The community council has delegated authority to decide.

title: Refusal of a Clothing Drop Box Location permit application located at 450 Rustic Road
topics: clothing drop boxes; clothes donation boxes; clothing bins
brief: This is a procedural item: Municipal Licensing and Standards refused an application for a clothing drop box location permit at 450 Rustic Road. The licensing director recommends that City Council deny the application.

title: Proposed Installation of Traffic Control Signals - Islington Avenue and Aviemore Drive

title: Kurdish Flag Raising
topics: executive committees, flag raising, motions; council decisions; decisions (council)
brief: On the evening of March 16, 1988, a horrific poisonous gas attack took place on the people of Halabja - for five hours a chemical attack was launched against the Kurdish people by Saddam Hussein. During the attack, more than 5,000 people lost their lives and more than 7,000 were injured and many more suffered lasting effects from birth defects, cancers and post-traumatic stress disorder. Councillor Jim Karygiannis, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford recommends that in recognition of the Halabja chemical attack, City Council amend the City of Toronto Flag Raising Policy to allow the Kurdish Flag to be raised every year in March, close to the commemoration day, at any courtesy flag pole in the City of Toronto to remember.

title: No Right Turn at O'Connor Drive and Four Oaks Gate
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: turn prohibitions (traffic);
brief: Dear Chair and Members of the Toronto and East York Community Council, Four Oaks Gate is a residential street just north of O'Connor Drive near Don Mills Road. title: Right-turns-on-red in Toronto
topics: motor vehicles, traffic, traffic speed, turn prohibitions (traffic); motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, vehicles
brief: There has been a growing call in many neighbourhoods across the City for restricting right-turns-on-red (RTOR), as one of many measures we can undertake through Vision Zero to make roads safer. Motor vehicle RTOR are a common type of collision in Toronto and is responsible for 13% of the city’s pedestrian injuries and/or fatalities. Councillor Mike Layton recommends that the Infrastructure and Environment Committee request the General Manager, Transportation Services provide an update on the status, and strategy to, proactively use right-turns-on-red prohibitions when reporting back on the effectiveness of speed limit reductions planned for the fourth quarter of 2020.

title: City of Toronto Support for Third-Party Community Fundraising Initiatives that Align with Goals and Priorities Established by City Council
brief: Earlier this year, my office was approached by The Survivors Fund, which requested that the City of Toronto join a number of corporate sponsors in supporting their upcoming gala fundraiser event through a financial commitment. As described on their website, "the gala dinner is targeting to raise over $200,000 in net dollars to be used in 2020 to provide interest-free loans to survivors of human trafficking and/or domestic violence." According to the organizers, every interest-free loan that helps a survivor to access appropriate housing saves the City of Toronto $3,000 per month over five months - or, in other words, frees up beds in our shelter system for others who need them. Councillor Joe Cressy recommends that The Economic and Community Development Committee request the Deputy City Manager, Community and Social Services, to undertake an immediate review of the request from The Survivors Fund with all relevant divisions and provide a formal response.

topics: history;
brief: Scarborough Community Council is asked to receive this presentation for information.
